chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Dinner at the Roosevelt and a horse of another color
summary: When the Senator invited them to the Roosevelt, Danny said they were Colored, and the Senator, thinking Lu was white, changed his plan.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, what happened, Paul said, "Man, that's wonderful, because Senator Lebeau has got gangs of station wagons. We were using Paul's little truck. That's before we got the bus. He had a little small station wagon. But it was hard carrying seven musicians and her. So we all piled up in this little...
We made a little thing like a wagon in the back of the station wagon.

We made a little trailer. So when Papa Stoppa... Senator Lebeau called me, he said... When he came in town the next day, that night, he said, "I want to take you and your wife to dinner at the Roosevelt. Well, that's how he come to invite us to the hotel. Because he said, "I want to take you and your wife to the Roosevelt Hotel for dinner, because I appreciate so much how you'all have made this thing be used as a jingle." So I said, "I don't think you can take us to the Roosevelt." He said, "Why? What's stopping you?" I said, "Because we're Colored." He said, "Oh, that's a horse of another color." Then he changed. He thought she was White.

He said, 'That's a horse of another color.' He said, 'I'll tell you what I'll do. You come down to the hotel...' That's why we went to the hotel. And that's why... He must have sent somebody to see who we were, standing there, and he must have been up there deciding what he was going to do. So he said, 'Come the next day.'
